hero.headline: Your data has a home now.
hero.sub: One lakehouse with dashboards built in. Bring every source in, keep it in open tables, and ask for answers in plain language.

sources.headline: Everything flows in.
sources.sub: Databases, files, streams, APIs and business apps land in one place, on a schedule or as they change.
sources.caption: Live change capture for PostgreSQL. Dedupe or keep history on load, discover tables in any source, and upload 10 files at once, in folders.

bronze.title: Raw, kept as it came.
bronze.body: Every source lands untouched in open Apache Iceberg tables, so nothing is lost and nothing is locked in.

silver.title: Cleaned and joined.
silver.body: Pipelines with schedules, dependencies, retries and version history clean the raw data into tables you can trust, and quality checks with anomaly detection watch them.

gold.title: Ready for answers.
gold.body: Curated tables built for the questions your business asks. They refresh themselves within the lag you set, and publish as open tables when you switch it on.

assistant.headline: Ask, don't dig.
assistant.sub: The assistant works with the same tools as the console. It answers questions, builds charts and dashboards, and runs pipelines. Anything risky waits for a person to approve it. Prefer SQL? Query Studio has autocomplete, tabs and a query history.
assistant.caption: Illustration
assistant.userOne: Which region had the most visitors last quarter?
assistant.answerOne: Region North had the most visitors last quarter.
assistant.srDescription: An illustration of the assistant. A person asks which region had the most visitors last quarter and the assistant answers with a small bar chart. The person then asks to pause the nightly sales pipeline, and the assistant shows a card that waits for a person to approve or decline the change. The region names and numbers are illustrative.

dashboards.headline: Answers come back up as dashboards.
dashboards.sub: About two dozen chart types, maps on your own boundaries included, with calculated fields, parameters, reusable metrics and results that are remembered and refreshed. Comment with @mentions, set alerts on a chart, export PNG, PDF or Excel, schedule reports, and share by a public link with an expiry and a password, or as an embed.
dashboards.caption: Illustrations, not customer data.

governance.headline: Guarded by default.
governance.sub: Roles decide who sees what. Sensitive columns are classified and masked for everyone who should not see them, and column-level lineage shows where every column comes from.
governance.tableCaption: Five fictional customers. As an analyst the name and email columns are masked; as an admin they are shown in full.
